method: Inspected the active-file constant, CLI choices, completion-set gate, unchanged canonical preparation and final preview/commit gate. Read the queue's explicit platform-file policy and confirmed the selected main TeX invokes the references BibTeX input. Verified final hashes. No key, private receipt contents, client, test, upload, network request or compiler was accessed/run by this reviewer.
findings: The platform-specific active upload set is exactly main.tex and references.bib. The generated main.bbl remains unchanged in the canonical three-descriptor release validation and receipt file-manifest fingerprint. No manuscript, bibliography, reference PDF or release manifest is rewritten by the adaptation.

The queue records the owner's actual unsupported-BBL registration outcome as the adaptation reason. The selected TeX uses bibliographystyle and bibliography{references}, so submitting the original TeX and BibTeX inputs is a valid source-packaging path; successful bibliography generation in the eventual remote PDF remains a required observed check, not an assumed result.

The CLI prevents new BBL registrations or byte uploads, and the completion/source-check gate now requires exactly the two active files with the existing paper/draft/upload/descriptor/hash associations. The unchanged three-descriptor fingerprint preserves associations of the already completed TeX/Bib uploads instead of inventing legacy receipt bindings.

Bound source-check/status GETs can now inspect the live two-file staged set. Preview POST and public commit remain hard-disabled before credentials; exact live path/hash/digest and later bibliography/preview checks are still prerequisites to their separate release. Fixed-origin secret protections, no automatic retries and the publication watchdog remain unchanged.
